texts: good. the walk, the base-of-the-cliff part-whole link, the morning and the past tense are all covered. One caveat on our side, not a phrasing problem: 'day 1 of Year 1' has no day-of-year slot in our time vocabulary, so it lands as (Day 1) beside (Year 1) — faithful to your figure, but in a slot that elsewhere means day-of-month.

good. the two assistants become a counted group walking with Tessa Brae as co-walker, and a per-member rule is laid down beside it so that naming one assistant later gives that assistant her own walk; the rule is fireable.

good. the three sky-cats become a counted group, 'during the hunt' nests the molting inside the hunt, and a fireable per-member rule hands the molting to each cat once one is named. One note on our side: the 'had' anteriority against the other sentences' events is not recorded — only the coarse past plus the during-link.

good. the fallen feathers become their own group and the base of the cliff is where they land, reusing the same base symbol as sentence 1. Again a note on our side: 'had fallen' is not ordered before the collecting in the next sentence, because our ordering test looks inside one sentence and your anteriority spans two, so a 'which came first' question will not resolve.

mixed: the collecting itself is faithful, but 'forty-one feathers' with no determiner mints a brand-new set of feathers — nothing in the parse says these are the ones that had fallen, so the two sets stay unconnected. If they are the molted feathers, make it a partitive: 'Tessa Brae collected forty-one of the fallen feathers at the base of the cliff.' — that records the forty-one as a subset of the earlier group.

good. the weighing reuses the collected forty-one feathers as its object and puts the Watch in the location slot; note only that a bare capitalized kind word like 'the Watch' is read as a common noun — a witness typed watch, with no name attached — which is our default.

mixed: 'a Watch ledger' is fused into a single kind symbol (watch_ledger, a kind of ledger), and a noun sitting inside a fused kind is never exposed as a link, so nothing connects the ledger to the Watch of the previous sentence and 'whose ledger was it?' cannot be answered. Write the relation out and the link lands: 'Tessa Brae recorded the feathers in a ledger of the Watch.'
good. the feathers — still the collected forty-one — are added with the feather bin as the destination, and the bin is typed as a kind of bin.
